newsitem.title: UK: Clarke confirms UK exempt from EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Clarke confirms UK exempt from EMU stability pact.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke confirmed on Tuesday that Britain would be exempted from a proposed stability pact aimed at limiting the budget deficits of members of the European Union's planned single currency.
Clarke was reporting to parliament on the outcome of a meeting of EU finance ministers he attended in Brussels on Monday.
Clarke confirms UK exempt from EMU stability =2
Clarke said he had obtained assurances from fellow finance ministers that membership of a proposed exchange rate mechanism for non-EMU members would be voluntary.

He said Britain had been committed to the convergence of economic and monetary policies necessary for the further development of the European Commuity ever since it signed the Single European Act in the mid-1980s.
"The present Treaty and practice only commit us to seek to ensure that our domestic policies are geared to price stability and sound public finances and to seek to avoid an excessive deficit.
"No sanctions can be applied to this country for any failure to take effective steps to achieve that unless and until we move to Stage 3 (of monetary union)," Clarke said.
